 Galveston County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0019
 Vincent Bryant, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Vincent Bryant
Date:
October 9, 2024
Location:
Offices of Conley & Stephenson Law Group
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Colleen Orr, Conley & Stephenson Law Group
Q: Plesae state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this matter. I'd prefer not to have my full name read into the transcript beyond what's
already on file.
Q: That's fine. Let's proceed. Can you describe how the collision happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward a shopping center. It was a clear afternoon. A vehicle
coming the other way drifted into my lane, and we ended up in a head-on collision. I hit the brakes, but there wasn't much time.
Q: How fast were you traveling at the moment of impact?
A: I'd guess I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour, nothing fancy. The other car wasn't going much faster. It wasn't a
high-speed crash by any means.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: The front airbags did deploy, yes. My head snapped forward and then back, and my neck felt it right away.
Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They checked me over, took X-rays, and told me I had a neck strain.
They gave me a cervical collar and some medication for the pain.
Q: Since that day, what treatment have you received?
A: I went to a physical therapist about two times a week for several weeks. I also did some stretching exercises at home. My
primary doctor checked on me a few times. The therapy helped some, but I still get stiffness when I turn my head quickly.
Q: How has the injury affected your daliy life?
A: Mostly it's the small things. I used to run errands and go to the gym most mornings. For a while I couldn't lift anything heavy,
and sleeping was harder because I couldn't find a comfortable position. I've had to take breaks when I'm driving, because looking
over my shoulder to change lanes can be uncomfortable.
Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I missed a few days right after the accident, and I was on light duty for a short period. I've been back to my normal schedule
for a while now.
Q: Do you have any pain today?
A: Some days are better than others. On bad days I get a dull ache at the base of my neck that goes up into my head. I manage it
with over-the-counter medication and heat packs.
</page>
